idle: Minus five point two. You said minus five. You were close.
(He points the infrared gun at the ice. Beep.)
good_ice: Minus five point one, centre ice. Minus five point three, the corners. Acceptable. Do not quote me.
bad_ice: Minus three point eight by the home bench. Somebody has been described, not measured.
wet_ice: Surface water. My gun does not like it. I do not like it.
cold: Cold is a number. Give me the number.
hungry: I will eat when the skates are dry.
bored: (He measures the boards. Then the bench. Then his coffee.)
goal: Good. Now the skates must be sharpened again.
greet_owner: Bonjour. What does your log say? Mine says minus five point two.
leaving_happy: The numbers agreed. Rare. I will tell Coach Rourke.
leaving_angry: The log had gaps. I have written down the gaps.

senior_hockey: Senior ice. I measure it anyway. For my own peace.

first.say: Rejean Paquette. Equipment, Duncannon Dukes, twenty-six years. (He points an infrared gun at your ice. It beeps.) Minus four point eight. What does your log say?

options.text: Let me check. Minus four point nine at the last round.

first_log.say: Point one apart. (He writes it down.) Close. Closer than most. We will see if you are close every time.

first_feels.say: Ice does not feel. Ice is a number. People feel. Usually wrong.

first_gun.say: You may see it. From there. (He does not move it any closer.) Nobody touches the gun.

options.text: I'm sorry. It'll be in the log next time.

say: Do not walk on my ice before the Dukes. I have measured it. If you walk on it, I have to measure it again.
Minus five point two, centre. Skates are dry. Acceptable. Go away, please. Politely.

trust.say: Your numbers and my numbers agree. Five rounds, two practices. I have told Coach Rourke. I do not tell Coach Rourke things lightly.

say: Yes? Quickly. The skates are drying.

options.text: What do you look for at a practice?
What do you make of our ice?

job.say: Twenty-six years. Skates, sticks, the skate room, the dryer. I have seen a hundred players go to Kingsport. Their skates were always dry. That is my contribution.

events.say: Practice ice that is the same every time. A dry skate room. A log with no gaps. And the Lumber Kings, on my night off, to measure somebody else's ice for pleasure.

gossip.say: Old Pete Vachon puts a hollow on a skate like nobody in the north. I will not say this to him. We discuss hollows. We have discussed hollows since 1999. And Coach Rourke is the only person I trust with the log.

rink.say: Your ice is {ice_word}. I want numbers. The Dukes practise at eighty-five or better, and the log must agree with my gun.

rink_better.say: (Beep. Beep. Beep.) Yes. Minus five point one, everywhere. Do not let it go to your head. Let it go to your log.

gun.say: Because people describe ice. 'Fast'. 'Good'. 'Fine'. My gun does not describe. My gun says minus five point two.

gun_measure.say: Good. Write it in the log. Every round. If you skip one, I will know. I will not say anything. I will look at you.
